Internal helper: resolve the which argument for jplot dispatch methods

Source: R/plot.R
dot-jst_resolve_which.Rd

Translates the user's which argument into a vector of plot identifiers. Accepts the special values core and all (resolved against the supplied core and all_plots vectors) or an explicit character vector of plot names. A name it does not take stops in voice Rule A's form, the result named by the function that made it, and the sentence of what which takes from .jst_takes_names() (Session 376).

Usage

.jst_resolve_which(which, core, all_plots, class_name, explain = NULL)

Arguments

which

The user's which argument: core, all, or a character vector of plot names.

core

Character vector of plot identifiers comprising the "core" set for this jplot method.

all_plots

Character vector of all valid plot identifiers for this jplot method.

class_name

Character. The S3 class being dispatched on; the stop names the function whose result it is.

explain

Optional named character vector: a plot name the method draws only for some results of its kind, and the stop that says why, used in place of the plot-name stop when that name is the only one refused (jcorr()'s scatter plot, which needs two variables).

Value

A character vector of plot identifiers to produce.

Details

A plot name typed without quotes (Fix Slate 23, Session 377) is read here, from the method's call, rather than evaluated: which = vif had stopped with R's own "object 'vif' not found". A name this result has gets ruling R18's pointer, the call with the name in quotes; a name it does not have gets the plot-name stop, since the pointer's line would stop on it next (ruling R23). The generic's own bare-word check leaves which to this helper whenever x is a result, so the set read is this result's, not every result's.
